analysis.reason: The paper identifies and characterizes NGC 5408 X-2 as an extreme, Compton-thick super-critical accretor/microquasar exhibiting relativistic jets ($L_{\rm radio} \sim 7.6\times 10^{35}\ {\rm erg\ s^{-1}}$) and a massive optically thick outflow with kinetic jet bubble power $P_{\rm k} \sim 2\times 10^{40}\ {\rm erg\ s^{-1}}$. It directly informs studies of compact object relativistic jets, photoionized nebulae, and circumstellar wind interactions.
analysis.result: The compact radio counterpart is variable and unresolved (size $\lesssim 20\ {\rm pc}$), peaking at $L_{\rm 5.5\,GHz} \approx 7.6\times 10^{35}\ {\rm erg\ s^{-1}}$ with a steep spectrum $S_{\nu} \propto \nu^{-\alpha}$ ($\alpha \approx 1.1 \pm 0.1$). Optical continuum is fit by an inflated blackbody with $T_{\rm bb} \approx 4600\ {\rm K}$, $R_{\rm bb} \approx 1700\ R_\odot$, and $L_{\rm bol} \approx 4.4\times 10^{39}\ {\rm erg\ s^{-1}}$, which faded by $\sim 2\ {\rm mag}$ between 2010 and 2024. Broad optical emission lines decreased in flux by a factor of $\sim 50$ (broad ${\rm H}\alpha$ dropped to $F({\rm H}\alpha) = (23\pm 2)\times 10^{-16}\ {\rm erg\ cm^{-2}\ s^{-1}}$ with FWHM narrowing from $\approx 1700$ to $\approx 1100\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$). A diffuse hot plasma bubble ($kT \approx 0.9\ {\rm keV}$, radius $\approx 1''$) implies shock kinetic power $P_{\rm k} \approx 2\times 10^{40} f^{1/2}\ {\rm erg\ s^{-1}}$, while narrow ${\rm He\ II}\ \lambda 4686$ emission requires an ionizing luminosity $L_{\rm ion} \sim 10^{40}\ {\rm erg\ s^{-1}}$, hidden along the line of sight by Compton-thick obscuration.
analysis.problem: Understanding the nature of an enigmatic compact source in NGC 5408 displaying extreme radio and optical luminosities, severe apparent X-ray faintness ($L_{\rm X} \lesssim 10^{38}\ {\rm erg\ s^{-1}}$), and an inflated cool optical photosphere exceeding stellar evolution limits.
analysis.method: Multi-epoch analysis combining ATCA/VLA radio imaging and spectral index fitting ($S_\nu \propto \nu^{-\alpha}$), HST optical aperture/PSF photometry, VLT/FORS2 and VLT/MUSE integral field spectroscopy for nebular line diagnostics and outflow kinematics, and Chandra ACIS-S sub-pixel imaging and spectral fitting (`apec + power-law`). Wind envelope scale is modeled via $R_{\rm w} \approx (3/2)(\kappa \dot{M}) / (4\pi v_{\rm w})$.
assumptions: The diffuse soft X-ray emitting plasma bubble is assumed to be in the Sedov-Taylor expansion phase driven by jet/wind kinetic power.
The central X-ray continuum engine is viewed at high inclination through Compton-thick obscuring material.
limits: Slit losses in legacy VLT/FORS2 observations prevent precise absolute continuum flux time-variability calibration from those spectra alone.
Radio observations cannot spatially resolve features below physical scales of $\lesssim 20\ {\rm pc}$.

analysis.reason: This paper focuses on galactic-scale 3D MHD simulations of cosmic-ray transport and spallation to explain the early Solar System 10Be/9Be abundance ratio recorded in meteorites. It does not address FRBs, PRS environments, relativistic jets, core-collapse supernova central engines, or high-energy transient phenomena.
analysis.result: The Galactic distribution of $^{10}\mathrm{Be}$ is overwhelmingly dominated by Galactic cosmic ray (GCR) spallation on ISM gas rather than direct SNR spallation (which contributes $\lesssim 10\%$ by volume and $\lesssim 1\%$ by gas mass). In newly formed stars (formed within 5 Myr), the inherited $^{10}\mathrm{Be}/^{9}\mathrm{Be}$ ratio is enhanced by a factor of $\sim 5$ compared to volume-weighted ISM gas due to spatial correlation with SN injection sites, yielding values consistent with the early Solar System meteoritic value $^{10}\mathrm{Be}/^{9}\mathrm{Be} \approx 7\times 10^{-4}$ under an enhanced star formation rate factor $\Psi = 2.0$ at the epoch of Solar System formation without requiring local irradiation.
analysis.problem: Whether the early Solar System abundance of short-lived radionuclide $^{10}\mathrm{Be}$ ($t_{1/2} = 1.387\ \mathrm{Myr}$), measured in CAIs to be $^{10}\mathrm{Be}/^{9}\mathrm{Be} \approx 7\times 10^{-4}$, originated from local irradiation by protosolar energetic particles or can be explained by inheritance from the parent molecular cloud permeated by Galactic cosmic rays.
analysis.method: Three-dimensional hydrodynamic AMR simulations using Enzo coupled with the Grackle cooling library and two-fluid cosmic ray transport with diffusion coefficient $\kappa_{\rm CR} = (1\text{--}10) \times 10^{28}\ \mathrm{cm}^2\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}$ on an AGORA-like isolated MW disc, tracking $^{10}\mathrm{Be}$ advection, radioactive decay, GCR spallation $P_{^{10}\mathrm{Be}}(\boldsymbol{x}) = P_{^{10}\mathrm{Be,Local}}[\epsilon_{\rm CR}(\boldsymbol{x})/\epsilon_{\rm CR,Local}]$, and SNR production scaled by $Q_{^{10}\mathrm{Be}} \simeq C_{^{10}\mathrm{Be}} n_{\rm H}$.
citation_leads: I Introduction: “Analyses of primitive inclusions in meteorites, such as calcium-aluminium-rich inclusions (CAIs) and chondrules, have revealed that the early Solar System was enriched in more than ten short-lived radionuclides”

II.5.1 GCR production of 10Be: “The production rate of 10Be per hydrogen atom, $P_{{}^{10}\mathrm{Be}}$ [atoms yr-1 H-1], is calculated by integrating the product of the differential GCR intensity and the spallation cross section over particle energy”

IV.1 Initial 10Be/9Be ratio and the Solar birth environment: “This suggests that inheritance of GCR-produced 10Be from the parent molecular cloud can account for the early Solar System’s 10Be/9Be without invoking a late injection or local irradiation.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrated via 3D galactic simulations that spatial clustering of star formation around cosmic-ray-injecting SNRs elevates inherited $^{10}\mathrm{Be}/^{9}\mathrm{Be}$ in star-forming cores by a factor of $\sim 5$ over one-zone diffuse ISM estimates, resolving the conflict between the inheritance scenario and meteoritic measurements.

analysis.result: By comparing the 511 keV gamma-ray flux produced by positron annihilation with INTEGRAL/SPI observations, the authors establish an upper limit of $N_{\rm max}=2.0\times 10^{52}$ on locally annihilated positrons per core collapse, deriving kinetic mixing constraints down to $\varepsilon \lesssim 10^{-14}$ for dark photons in the mass window $1\,\mathrm{MeV}\lesssim m_{A'}\lesssim 3\,\mathrm{MeV}$.
analysis.reading_entry: Presupernovae Strongly Constrain Electrophilic MeV Bosons
analysis.problem: Constraining electrophilic MeV bosons from supernova explosions is severely limited by high plasma frequencies ($\omega_{\rm pl}\sim 10\,\mathrm{MeV}$) causing in-medium kinetic mixing suppression $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{eff},T} \simeq \varepsilon m_{A^{\prime}}^2 / |m_{A^{\prime}}^2 - \omega_{\rm pl}^2|$, as well as the very short burst duration of the explosion core.
analysis.method: Using MESA models for $9\text{--}60\,M_\odot$ stars, the authors evaluate boson production via $e^+ e^- \to A^{\prime}$ coalescence with rate $dN_{A^{\prime}}/(dV dt) = \frac{\alpha \varepsilon^2 (m_{A^{\prime}}^2 + 2m_e^2) T \sqrt{m_{A^{\prime}}^2 - 4m_e^2}}{2\pi^2} K_1(m_{A^{\prime}}/T)$, convolving the yield with a Salpeter IMF ($dN/dM\propto M^{-2.35}$), Galactic progenitor distributions, and a smearing scale $\lambda_{\rm sm}$ for positron diffusion against INTEGRAL/SPI 511 keV measurements.
assumptions: Dark photon emission causes negligible stellar backreaction when QA'/Qnu <= 10^-2.
limits: Constraints are subject to astrophysical uncertainties in the positron smearing length lambda_sm.

analysis.result: The blazar's X-ray spectrum resolves into two distinct emission components: a soft component with photon index $\Gamma \gtrsim 2.5$ dominant at $E < 2\,\mathrm{keV}$ that fades within $\sim 14\,\mathrm{h}$, and a hard component with $\Gamma \sim 1.7-1.9$ dominant at $E > 2\,\mathrm{keV}$ that subsequently brightens by a factor of $\sim 1.5$. analysis.reason: This work uses spatially-resolved IXPE X-ray polarization modeling to measure magnetic turbulence in the SS 433 eastern jet, directly probing relativistic jet-medium shear interactions relevant to compact object high-energy outflows.
analysis.result: The eastern extended X-ray jet shows uniform electric vector position angles (EVPA $\sim 0^\circ$) perpendicular to the $\sim 94^\circ$ jet axis, establishing jet-aligned magnetic fields. The sheath exhibits suppressed polarization relative to the head and spine ($>3.2\sigma$ multi-zone improvement over single-zone), corresponding to enhanced turbulence $\tau = \delta B / B_0 \gtrsim 1.8$ compared to $\tau \lesssim 1.5$ in the spine and head (a factor of $\sim 2$ increase). For a photon index $\Gamma = 1.54$, the theoretical synchrotron maximum polarization is $\Pi_0 = \Gamma / (\Gamma + 2/3) \approx 69.8\%$, and the inferred post-shock flow yields an Alfvén Mach number $M_{\rm A} = 1300 \times (\frac{v}{0.08c}) (\frac{B}{12\,\mu\mathrm{G}})^2 (\frac{0.2\,\mathrm{cm}^{-3}}{n_{\rm H}})^2 \gg 1$, proving magnetic tension cannot stabilize shear flows.
analysis.problem: Resolving whether the reduced X-ray polarization in the SS 433 eastern jet boundary is caused by macroscopic magnetic field reversals or boundary-layer shear turbulence generated by jet-ambient interactions.
analysis.method: Event-by-event unbinned maximum likelihood fitting in Stokes $q$-$u$ space using LeakageLib to eliminate Ricean bias, incorporating high-resolution Chandra spatial and spectral templates across 2–8 keV to segment the jet into head, spine, and sheath components, and modeling turbulence via $\tau = \delta B / B_0 = \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}\frac{\Pi_0 - {\rm PD}}{{\rm PD}}} \sin i$.

IV.2 Physical Interpretation: “The decreased sheath PD is naturally interpreted as an increase in magnetic turbulence generated at the jet boundary, with $\tau$ roughly $2\times$ larger than in the head or spine.”
analysis.research_progress: Provides the first spatially resolved observational constraint demonstrating that magnetic turbulence is roughly twice as strong in the jet sheath ($\tau \gtrsim 1.8$) as in the spine ($\tau \lesssim 1.5$), providing direct evidence for Kelvin-Helmholtz instability-driven turbulence at microquasar jet boundaries.

analysis.reason: This study analyzes the interaction between compact relativistic jets and the ISM using DESI and VLASS data, establishing that small, confined jets drive strong radiative shocks that perturb gas kinematics and dominate ionization over photoionization.
analysis.result: Small-scale radio sources ($10\,\mathrm{kpc} \le D \le 15\,\mathrm{kpc}$) exhibit significantly broader $[\mathrm{O\,III}]$ profiles (median $W80 = 694\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ vs $518\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ for large sources $D \ge 25\,\mathrm{kpc}$, with an extreme tail $W80 > 1300\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ exclusively in small sources), lower $[\mathrm{Ne\,V}]\,\lambda 3426$ detection rates ($30\%$ vs $58\%$ at $>3\sigma$), and systematic displacement toward LINER-like emission-line ratios, driven by jet kinetic power $Q \simeq 3\times 10^{38}\,f^{3/2}(L_{151}/10^{28}\,\mathrm{W\,Hz^{-1}\,sr^{-1}})^{6/7}\,\mathrm{W}$.
analysis.problem: Distinguishing whether the perturbed kinematics and optical emission line ionization in compact radio galaxies are governed by radiative accretion-disk photoionization or by fast radiative shocks driven directly into the multiphase ISM by confined jets.
analysis.method: Cross-matched VLASS with DESI DR1 ($0.15 < z < 0.5$) applying a cut $L_{\rm 3\,GHz} > 10^{24}\,\mathrm{W\,Hz^{-1}}$ to yield 44 small ($10\text{--}15\,\mathrm{kpc}$) and 33 large ($\ge 25\,\mathrm{kpc}$) sources; performed multi-Gaussian decomposition on optical emission lines to measure kinematic broadening $W80$, BPT line diagnostics ($[\mathrm{O\,I}]/\mathrm{H}\alpha$ vs $[\mathrm{O\,III}]/\mathrm{H}\beta$), and compared against jet kinetic power $Q$ scaling relations.

III Results: “The small sources have broader [O iii] profiles, and the extreme tail above 1300 km s-1 belongs entirely to the small sample.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates empirically that compact radio sources confined within host galaxy ISM are dominated by strong shocks ($v_{\rm shock} \gtrsim 600\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$) rather than disk photoionization, providing clean observational diagnostics to differentiate jet-ISM interactions from unconfined CGM propagation.

analysis.reason: This work extends the open-source 3D Monte Carlo radiative transfer code SKIRT to compute photon arrival time lags, providing a self-consistent tool for high-energy reverberation mapping and echo studies in complex compact object environments.
analysis.result: The code successfully recovers time lag distributions in arbitrary 3D geometries. In optically thick media, late-time transmission lags decay exponentially as $F_{\mathrm{t}}(t) \propto \exp(-\tau_{\mathrm{es}} c \,\delta t / D)$, with the mean time lag $\langle\delta t\rangle$ converging to the skin-depth lag $\delta t_{0.5} \equiv 2 d_{0.5}/c$. Owing to $\sigma_{\mathrm{PA}}(E) \propto E^{-3}$, neutral Fe K$\alpha$ fluorescence ($6.38\text{--}6.42\ \mathrm{keV}$, threshold $7.112\ \mathrm{keV}$) penetrates deeper and exhibits longer arrival delays than the continuum, producing a peak reverberation lag $\tau_{\mathrm{peak}} \approx 2.39 \times 10^6\ \mathrm{s}$ ($\approx 28\ \mathrm{d}$) for an AGN torus model around a $M_\bullet = 10^7 M_\odot$ black hole. Simulation efficiency is characterized by $\mathrm{FOM} \equiv 1 / (R^2 T)$ with convergence criteria $R < 0.1$ and $\mathrm{VOV} < 0.1$.

analysis.problem: Self-consistently calculating energy-dependent photon arrival time lags, reverberation transfer functions, and Compton echo profiles across complex, non-spherical 3D circumstellar and circumnuclear media around high-energy compact objects.
analysis.method: Implemented path-length accumulation in 3D Monte Carlo code SKIRT: photon packets track cumulative spatial path $\mathcal{D} \coloneqq \mathcal{D} + |\mathbf{r}_{i} - \mathbf{r}_{i-1}|$, with peel-off emission corrected for coordinate origin projection $\mathcal{D} \coloneqq -\mathbf{\hat{n}}_{\mathrm{obs}}\cdot\mathbf{r}_0$ and exit lag $\delta t = (\mathcal{D} - \mathbf{\hat{n}}_{\mathrm{obs}} \cdot \mathbf{r}_{i})/c$. Handled Klein-Nishina electron scattering and photoelectric absorption with Fe K$\alpha$ fluorescence, and convolved transfer functions with damped random walk (DRW) light curves to compute cross-correlation functions (CCF).

analysis.reason: This paper evaluates the impact of updated Bayesian carbon-fusion rates and carbon-helium rates on white-dwarf heating and the pair-instability black-hole mass boundary, providing crucial nuclear inputs for compact object formation and supernova progenitor modeling.
analysis.result: For accreting carbon-oxygen white dwarfs at $\dot{M} = 10^{-7}\,M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, the Bayesian median rate delays the thermal equilibrium $L_{\rm nuc} = L_{\nu} + L_{\gamma}$, yielding a central temperature $\sim 2.57\%$ higher and central density $18.9\%$ higher than standard CF88 rates. In $20\,M_{\odot}$ stars at core carbon exhaustion, the updated rates and branching increase ${}^{20}\mathrm{Ne}$ retained mass by $+10.78\%$ and decrease ${}^{23}\mathrm{Na}$ by $-28.70\%$. analysis.reason: This work explores black hole spin evolution and equilibrium spin limits using GRMHD simulations across various magnetic field geometries, providing key constraints on central engine efficiency and relativistic jet launching.
analysis.result: Using 2D GRMHD simulations across $\chi \in [0, 0.99]$, the equilibrium spin $\chi_{\rm eq}$ (where $\langle\dot{\chi}\rangle = 0$ for $\dot{\chi} = \dot{J}_h/M^2 - 2\chi\dot{M}_h/M$) is shown to depend sensitively on magnetic topology: a fiducial model ($\beta_{\max} = 100$) reaches $\chi_{\rm eq} \simeq 0.88$, multiple loops give $\chi_{\rm eq} \simeq 0.87$, strong magnetic fields ($\beta_{\max} = 10$) rapidly disrupt the torus shifting turnover to $\chi \in [0.37, 0.71]$, while radially modulated magnetic flux permits near-extremal spin $\chi_{\rm eq} \simeq 0.98$. The physical spin evolution rate scales as $\dot{\chi}^{\rm phys} \approx 2\times 10^{-8} f_{\rm Edd}\dot{\chi}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, implying evolution timescales $>10^{13}\,{\rm yr}$ for Sgr A* under its current low accretion rate.
analysis.reading_entry: How Fast do Black Holes Spin?
analysis.problem: How magnetic stresses across the ISCO and jet angular momentum extraction modify the equilibrium spin $\chi_{\rm eq}$ and spin evolution of accreting black holes relative to the standard Novikov-Thorne thin-disk radiative capture limit ($\chi_{\rm eq} \simeq 0.998$).
analysis.method: Axisymmetric GRMHD simulations using BHAC in fixed Kerr spacetime with Fishbone-Moncrief equilibrium tori (adiabatic index $\Gamma = 4/3$, specific angular momentum $\ell = u_\phi/u_t$, and effective potential $W(r,\theta)$), seeding poloidal magnetic fields via vector potential $A_\phi(r,\theta) = [\rho(r,\theta) - \rho_{\rm cut}]_+ f_\theta(\theta) f_r(r)$ normalized by $\beta_{\max} = p_{\max}/(b_{\max}^2/2)$, and extracting horizon mass flux $\dot{M}_h$ and angular momentum flux $\dot{J}_h$ to measure $\dot{\chi} = \dot{J}_h/M^2 - 2\chi\dot{M}_h/M$.
citation_leads: How Fast do Black Holes Spin?: “extract the mass flux and angular momentum flux through the horizon to compute the time-averaged spin evolution rate”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates that GRMHD accretion disk torques generally suppress $\chi_{\rm eq}$ to $\sim 0.87\text{--}0.88$ below the Thorne limit, yet specific radial flux modulations can maintain near-extremal spins up to $\chi_{\rm eq} \simeq 0.98$, with physical scaling $\dot{\chi}^{\rm phys} \approx 2\times 10^{-8} f_{\rm Edd}\dot{\chi}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$.

analysis.result: Dynamic collapse of a hadronic neutron star triggered by deconfinement can occur despite the existence of radially stable hybrid star configurations with identical baryon mass $M_B$, lowering the black hole formation threshold by $\Delta M_B \approx 0.12\,M_\odot$ below the static threshold. analysis.problem: The long-term rotational torque variations, pulse profile restructuring, and component-dependent short-timescale mode-changing transitions in the magnetosphere of the radio magnetar Swift J1818.0$-$1607 following its 2020 outburst.
analysis.method: Simultaneous dual-frequency (2.25 GHz and 8.60 GHz) observations using the Tianma 65-m Radio Telescope (TMRT) with the DIBAS backend; piecewise timing analysis with TEMPO2; profile decomposition using multiple Gaussian components; Hidden Markov Models (HMM) with Bayesian Information Criterion ($\Delta\mathrm{BIC} \ge 10$) and Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to detect and classify mode transitions; two-point spectral index computation $\alpha = \ln(S_{8.60}/S_{2.25})/\ln(8.60/2.25)$ and radiometric flux calibration via receiver SEFD.

analysis.reason: This work quantitatively computes one-loop QED dispersion relations and time delays for photons traversing magnetized vacuum and degenerate plasma in neutron star magnetospheres, revealing that vacuum birefringence induces delays of $\sim 10-10^3\ \mathrm{ns}$ while plasma medium effects can reach milliseconds in the X-ray band.
analysis.result: In the weak-field limit ($eB \ll m_e^2$), the vacuum phase velocities scale as $v_V^{\mathrm{WF},(1,2)} \approx 1 - \frac{\alpha}{90\pi}\left(\frac{B}{B_c}\right)^2$ and $v_V^{\mathrm{WF},(3)} \approx 1 - \frac{\alpha}{30\pi}\left(\frac{B}{B_c}\right)^2$, whereas in the strong-field limit ($eB \gg m_e^2$), mode 3 saturates to $v_V^{\mathrm{SF},(3)} \approx 1 - \frac{\alpha}{3\pi}$ independent of $B$ due to lowest Landau level dominance. For magnetar magnetospheres, the integrated propagation delay in Schwarzschild spacetime, $\Delta\tau = \int_{r_0}^{r_0+L} dr \left(\frac{1}{v_p} - 1\right) \left(1 - \frac{2M}{r}\right)^{-1}$, yields nanosecond-to-microsecond delays for pure vacuum QED ($\,\Delta\tau_V \sim 10-10^3\ \mathrm{ns}\,$, reducing by a factor of 5 when transitioning from toroidal to dipole decay), whereas the degenerate electron-positron medium contribution reaches the millisecond scale ($\Delta\tau_M \sim 10^{-1}-10^2\ \mathrm{ms}$) at X-ray frequencies $\hbar\omega \sim 1-100\ \mathrm{keV}$.

analysis.reason: The paper develops and benchmarks an autonomous multi-agent pipeline with strict provenance validation for high-energy astrophysics data reduction, demonstrating high fidelity on IXPE polarimetric observations of black hole X-ray binaries.
analysis.result: The pipeline reproduced published IXPE polarimetric measurements of Cyg X-1 with all 14 quantities agreeing within $3\sigma$ (polarization angle deviation $<0.5\sigma$; energy dependence slope in ${\rm PD}(E)=A+B\,(E/\mathrm{keV}-1)$ within $0.24\sigma$, while polarization degrees were offset by $0.2$--$2.4\sigma$). analysis.reason: The paper demonstrates that 3D radiative relativistic magnetic reconnection in black hole coronae can simultaneously self-regulate pair loading, produce seed photons, and account for the observed MeV tail in X-ray binaries like Cygnus X-1.
analysis.result: Free particles escaping flux ropes in 3D relativistic reconnection accelerate to the synchrotron burnoff limit ($\sim 16\,\mathrm{MeV}$), yielding a ratio of synchrotron to inverse Compton power $\xi \sim 0.25\text{--}0.5$ (up to $0.5\text{--}0.9$ with full cooling). In a corona of size $R \sim 2 \times 10^6 \sqrt{1+\xi}\,\mathrm{cm}$ and magnetic field $B \sim 10^8\,\mathrm{G}$, high-energy $\gamma$-rays experience $\gamma\gamma$ absorption with optical depth $\tau_{\gamma\gamma} \simeq 40 (\varepsilon_1 / 100\,\mathrm{keV})^{-0.7} (\varepsilon_\gamma / m_e c^2)^{0.3}$ for $\varepsilon_\gamma \gg (m_e c^2)^2/\varepsilon_1 \simeq 2.6\,\mathrm{MeV}$. This attenuates the emission above $\varepsilon_{\rm tail} \simeq 1.5\,\mathrm{MeV}$ to $\varepsilon L_\varepsilon \propto \varepsilon^{-1.2}$, matching the observed MeV tail, while secondary pairs supply a Thomson depth $\tau_T^\pm \sim 2 B_8^2 R_{6.5}$ and emit self-absorbed synchrotron peaking at $\varepsilon_{\rm SSA} \simeq 0.13\,\mathrm{keV}$ that self-consistently fuels Comptonization when $\xi > \xi_s^{\rm num} \simeq 0.1$.
analysis.reading_entry: II.2 Energy scales of the accelerated particles
analysis.problem: Standard Comptonization models for black hole X-ray binaries in the hard state lack a self-consistent mechanism to supply seed soft photons, load pairs into the corona, and explain the non-thermal MeV tail alongside the $\sim 100\,\mathrm{keV}$ thermal-like peak within a single coronal zone.
analysis.method: Theoretical scaling analysis coupled with 3D radiative kinetic particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations using Tristan v2 (magnetization $\sigma=10$, guide field $B_g=0.1B$, reconnection rate $\beta_{\rm rec} \approx 0.07\text{--}0.08$, with combined inverse Compton and synchrotron damping forces switching at $\gamma_{\rm SSA}$), followed by steady-state radiation transport modeling using the LeHaMoC code.
assumptions: Synchrotron radiation from particles with $\gamma < \gamma_{\rm SSA}$ is suppressed by self-absorption, leaving inverse Compton scattering as their dominant cooling channel.
citation_leads: Radiative relativistic reconnection powering the hard-state emission of X-ray binaries: synchrotron-driven pair loading, MeV tail, and seed photons: “In 3D reconnection, so-called “free” particles escape the flux ropes and accelerate at the maximum rate set by the reconnection electric field.”
II.2 Energy scales of the accelerated particles: “Synchrotron radiation from particles below the self-absorption threshold $\gamma_{\text{SSA}}$ is self-absorbed.”

III.2 Optical depth of $gammagammarightarrow e^-e^+$ interactions: “The corona is therefore optically thick to $\gamma\gamma$ pair production for $\gamma$-rays above $\sim 2.6$ MeV, with the opacity increasing toward higher energies.”

IV.1 PIC setup: “We perform a suite of 3D radiative kinetic simulations of relativistic reconnection in electron–positron plasma using the particle-in-cell (PIC) code Tristan v2 on a uniform Cartesian grid”

V.2.1 Fiducial model: “above $\varepsilon_{\text{tail}}$, the attenuated spectrum follows a power law, $\varepsilon L_{\varepsilon}\propto\varepsilon^{-1.2}$. The overall shape of the photon spectrum above $\sim 1\,\text{MeV}$ is consistent with the MeV emission”
analysis.research_progress: Moves beyond 2D plasmoid-chain reconnection by leveraging 3D flux-rope escape of accelerated leptons to reach synchrotron energies above tens of MeV, self-consistently explaining the MeV tail slope $\varepsilon L_\varepsilon \propto \varepsilon^{-1.2}$ via $\gamma\gamma$ absorption while naturally providing pair loading $\tau_T^\pm \sim 1$ and internal seed photons for Comptonization.

analysis.reason: The study develops a discretized numerical framework for gradually accelerating, magnetically dissipative relativistic jets from supermassive black holes, showing that magnetic reconnection yields synchrotron-dominated SEDs where inverse Compton scattering is strongly suppressed due to $U'_B \gg U'_e$.
analysis.result: The model demonstrates that gradual magnetic dissipation produces synchrotron-dominated emission across the entire jet, with a Compton dominance $L_{\rm ICS}/L_{\rm syn} \sim 10^{-3}$ matching the comoving energy density ratio $U'_B / U'_e \sim 10^3$. Bulk acceleration and dissipation scale as $\Gamma(z) \propto z^{1/3}$, $\sigma(z) \propto z^{-1/3}$, and $z\frac{\mathrm{d}L_{\rm diss}}{\mathrm{d}z} \propto z^{1/3}$. Accounting for inter-segment photon spillage enhances the inverse Compton scattering luminosity by a factor of $\approx 3$. External photon fields (e.g., BLR) fail to produce high Compton dominance unless extreme bulk Lorentz factors $\Gamma_{\infty} \gtrsim 130$ are assumed.
analysis.problem: Whether continuous magnetic reconnection in striped relativistic jets can self-consistently reproduce the diverse broadband spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of blazars and how radiative transfer between differentially accelerating jet segments affects inverse Compton signatures.
analysis.method: A continuous relativistic jet undergoing bulk acceleration governed by $\Gamma(z)(1+\sigma(z)) \approx \Gamma_\infty$ is discretized into comoving segments using the LeHaMoC code. Non-thermal electrons are injected with $Q'_e(\gamma', z') = Q'_0(z')\gamma'^{-s}$ up to the synchrotron-cooling limited Lorentz factor $\gamma'_{\max} = \sqrt{6\pi e/(\eta_{\rm acc}\sigma_{\rm T}B')} \propto z^{2/3}$, iteratively solving radiative transfer and inter-segment photon irradiation accounting for relative Lorentz factors $\Gamma_{\rm rel} = \Gamma_i\Gamma_j(1 - \beta_i\beta_j)$ and $\gamma\gamma$ opacity.
citation_leads: Electromagnetic signatures of gradual magnetic dissipation in jets from supermassive black holes: “Gradual magnetic dissipation in jets from supermassive black holes leads to nearly universal, synchrotron-dominated photon spectra.”
3 Description of the numerical jet model: “The continuous jet is discretized into segments, each of which has its own rest frame, since $\Gamma$ increases with $z$.”
4.1 Jet emission: “This calculation neglects potential contributions from other segments to a segment’s local photon density.”
6 Conclusions: “Inter-segment radiation spillage produces some power transfer effects, by a factor of three, in the part of the spectrum affected by inverse Compton scattering.”
A.2 Relative motion of segments: “In the gradual dissipation jet model each segment has different Lorentz factor due to the continuous bulk acceleration of the jet plasma.”
analysis.research_progress: Constructed an iterative multi-segment radiative transfer model that captures continuous jet bulk acceleration, demonstrating that inter-segment photon spillage yields a modest $\sim 3\times$ boost in inverse Compton flux, confirming that steady-state magnetic reconnection jets remain heavily synchrotron-dominated throughout the parsec to kiloparsec scales.

analysis.reason: The paper presents comprehensive multi-wavelength observations and shock-CSM interaction modeling for the luminous Type IIn SN 2019qem, constraining pre-supernova mass loss and shock dynamics.
analysis.result: SN 2019qem peaked at $M_I = -20.49_{-0.03}^{+0.01}\,\mathrm{mag}$ with $L_{\rm peak} = (7.0 \pm 0.4) \times 10^{43}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and radiated $E_{\rm opt} = 6.9 \times 10^{50}\,\mathrm{erg}$ over 575 d. Thin-shell modeling prefers an ejecta mass $M_{\mathrm{ej}} = 7.0_{-0.9}^{+1.4}\,M_{\odot}$, kinetic energy $E_{\mathrm{K}} = 5.2_{-1.4}^{+3.6} \times 10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$ ($E_{\mathrm{K}} \epsilon = [3.5 \pm 0.3] \times 10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$), an eruptive CSM shell $M_{\mathrm{er}} \approx 9.3\,M_{\odot}$, and a steady wind mass-loss rate $\dot{M}_{w} = 0.62_{-0.15}^{+0.24}\,M_{\odot}\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$ (for $v_w = 100\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$), indicating a progenitor zero-age main-sequence mass $M_{\rm ZAMS} \gtrsim 40\,M_{\odot}$.
analysis.problem: Unraveling the extreme mass-loss mechanism and CSM geometry in massive stars decades before core collapse, and breaking the severe degeneracy between shock velocity $v_{\mathrm{sh}}$ and wind density $\dot{M}/v_w$ when interpreting collisionally powered light curves.
analysis.method: Multi-band optical (OGLE, LCO), mid-infrared (NEOWISE), and spectroscopy (SALT, NTT, VLT) were analyzed using Bayesian light-curve fitting with the REDBACK thin-shell model (shock luminosity scaling as $L \propto \epsilon [\dot{M}/v_w] v_{\mathrm{sh}}^3$), semi-analytic self-similar interaction solutions, and multi-component profile decompositions of the $\mathrm{H}\alpha$ line.
assumptions: The pre-supernova wind expansion velocity is assumed to be $v_w = 100\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ when converting wind density parameter to $\dot{M}$.
limits: Light curve modeling alone cannot independently break the parameter degeneracy between shock velocity and CSM density without spectroscopic velocity constraints from lines.

analysis.reason: The paper provides an improved theoretical framework combining two-body diffusion and collisionless chaotic diving orbits in flattened galactic potentials, yielding a key boost factor $1 + \ln(j_d/j_t)$ to tidal disruption event (TDE) rates.
analysis.result: Disruption rates in flattened potentials are enhanced over the classical loss-cone rate $\Gamma_{\rm cl}$ by a multiplicative factor $\Gamma / \Gamma_{\rm cl} \approx 1 + \ln(j_d / j_t)$, typically yielding an order-of-magnitude increase ($\sim 10\times$) for characteristic chaotic diving thresholds $j_d \gtrsim 0.1$. When diffusion is weak ($\sigma \lesssim 0.1 j_t$), disruptions are highly anisotropic and aligned near the disk plane ($|\cos i| \to 1$), while in the well-mixed regime ($\sigma \gtrsim j_t$), the penetration factor distribution follows $p(\beta) \propto \beta^{-2}$.
analysis.problem: Classical loss-cone theory based solely on two-body relaxation underestimates disruption rates by omitting chaotic orbit migration, whereas previous collisionless chaotic models neglected depletion of the diving region and diffusion coupling, hindering self-consistent equilibrium predictions.
analysis.method: The authors construct a 2D equilibrium Fokker-Planck model $p(j_z, j)$ coupling two-body scattering, rapid uniform chaotic redistribution within diving orbits ($j < j_d$), and pericenter loss ($j < j_t$), supplemented by 1D/2D analytical Bessel solutions and walker-based Monte Carlo simulations.
citation_leads: 2 The loss cone and the loss wedge: “Thus any system with $j_{z}<j_{t}$ and $j<j_{d}$ has a chance of disruption from chaotic angular momentum redistribution alone.”
4.1 Total rate and separability: “We seek a fixed-point solution: a distribution $p(j_{z},j)$ that is unchanged after one full cycle of scattering, diving, loss, and renormalisation.”
5.4.2 Comparing to $Gammacl$: “Another benchmark to compare to is how much the inclusion of the diving region boosts the rate of disruptions compared to the classical case.”

6 Discussion and Conclusions: “We present analytical arguments and toy models that estimate the boost to disruption rates, $\Gamma$, compared to the classical case which ignores diving orbits, $\Gamma_{cl}$, of approximately $\Gamma/\Gamma_{cl}\sim 1+\ln(j_{d}/j_{t})”
analysis.research_progress: Establishes a unified analytical and numerical loss-cone formalism that self-consistently couples two-body scattering with chaotic phase-space mixing, proving the robust scaling $\Gamma / \Gamma_{\rm cl} \approx 1 + \ln(j_d / j_t)$ and determining the resulting orientation and penetration distributions.

analysis.reason: This paper investigates whether low-mass binary black hole events like GW241011 and GW241110 are naturally expected within hierarchical merger channels and formulates likelihood-ratio classification metrics across spin-precession parameter space.
analysis.result: Hierarchical mergers (1G+2G) are classified via likelihood ratio metrics: in simulated realistic cluster (CMC) mergers, the $\chi_{\mathrm{p}}$ metric alone achieves a $24\%$ ($182$ events) classification rate, whereas a joint $(\chi_{\mathrm{eff}}, \chi_{\mathrm{p}})$ metric increases identification to $35\%$ ($265$ events) by eliminating face-on selection vulnerability. Binary mass ratio $q$ is identified as the dominant intrinsic driver of identification over primary mass $m_{1,\mathrm{det}}$, with unequal-mass binaries ($q \lesssim 0.4$) dramatically improving precession measurement precision.

analysis.reason: The study directly constrains the delay-time distribution (DTD) of binary neutron star mergers, showing an unexpected preference for multi-Gyr delay times that challenges standard isolated binary evolution models and impacts kilonova and short gamma-ray burst progenitor rates.
analysis.result: The stellar population analysis of NGC 4993 yields a mass-weighted age of $12.4^{+0.5}_{-0.7}\,\mathrm{Gyr}$. Under an efficiency-normalized power-law DTD model ($\mathrm{DTD} = A t^{\alpha}$), the minimum delay time is constrained to $t_{\rm min} > 7.5\pm 0.2\,\mathrm{Gyr}$ (90% credible level) and $t_{\rm min} > 5.6\pm 0.2\,\mathrm{Gyr}$ (95% credible level), peaking at $12.6\pm 0.7\,\mathrm{Gyr}$ for $\alpha = -1$. The empirical $(12.6\,\mathrm{Gyr}, -1)$ model is favored over the canonical $(10\,\mathrm{Myr}, -1)$ model by a Bayes/likelihood factor of 41–138.

analysis.problem: Standard binary neutron star evolution predicts a delay-time distribution $dN/dt \propto t^{-1}$ with $t_{\rm min} \sim 10\,\mathrm{Myr}$, implying that short-delay mergers should outnumber long-delay mergers by $\sim 16:1$, creating a severe statistical tension with GW170817 originating in an extremely old stellar population.
analysis.method: The host galaxy NGC 4993 was analyzed using prospector and FSPS with MIST isochrones and MILES spectral libraries across 14 photometric bands and VLT/MUSE integral field spectroscopy to reconstruct its non-parametric star formation history (SFH). Poisson likelihood frameworks incorporating cosmic star formation history $\psi(t)$ and DTD parameterizations ($A t^\alpha$) were evaluated via nested sampling with dynesty.

analysis.reason: This work develops the ARISE framework linking binary black hole (BBH) mergers in AGN disks to cosmological AGN and SMBH growth, providing testable merger rates and population predictions for current LVK observations and next-generation gravitational wave detectors like the Einstein Telescope.
analysis.result: The local comoving merger rate density is primarily governed by the disk viscosity parameter $\alpha$: at $z=0.2$, $\mathcal{R}(z=0.2)=24^{+13}_{-8}\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ for $\alpha=0.01$ (peaking at $z\simeq 1.8$ at $280^{+170}_{-110}\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$), whereas $\alpha=0.1$ reduces the rates by roughly an order of magnitude to $0.5\text{--}6\,\mathrm{Gpc^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$ ($f_{\mathrm{AGN}}\sim 2\%\text{--}38\%$), making $\alpha=0.1$ consistent with empirical electromagnetic flare upper limits ($f_{\mathrm{AGN}}\lesssim 40\%$). For the Einstein Telescope ($T_{\mathrm{obs}}=1\,\mathrm{yr}$, SNR $\rho>12$), expected detections reach $0.9\text{--}1.6\times 10^5$ events for $\alpha=0.01$ and $\sim 10^4$ for $\alpha=0.1$, with super-Eddington models (CAT-SE) predicting persistent detections out to $z\simeq 8$.
analysis.problem: Current ground-based gravitational wave detectors only observe stellar-mass BBH mergers out to $z\sim 1.5$, leaving the high-redshift ($z\gtrsim 2\text{--}10$) evolution of BBH merger rates, their connection to SMBH accretion pathways (Eddington-limited vs. super-Eddington), and the fraction of LVK mergers produced in AGN disks unconstrained.
analysis.method: The ARISE framework couples a semi-analytic AGN disk dynamical model (FastClusterAGN accounting for Type I/II migration, gas damping, pairing with semi-major axis distribution $p(a)\propto a^{9/2}$, and gravitational wave hardening) with cosmological semi-analytic models of SMBH growth (CAT-EL and CAT-SE). Source-frame merger rate densities $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{AGN}}(z)$ are computed by integrating the mean galaxy merger rate $\bar{\Gamma}$ weighted by the comoving active AGN number density $n_{\mathrm{AGN}}(z)$ and active fraction $f_{\mathrm{active}}(M_\bullet, z)=\frac{\int_{\dot{M}_{\bullet,\mathrm{min}}}^\infty d\dot{M}_\bullet\,\Phi}{\int_0^\infty d\dot{M}_\bullet\,\Phi}$.
assumptions: Hierarchical BH growth terminates only if the cumulative merger timescale exceeds the disk lifetime $\tau$, a recoil kick ejects the remnant, or local BH seeds are exhausted.
limits: Disk physics neglects complex 3D magnetohydrodynamic turbulence and disk-wind mass loss, relying on 1D Sirko & Goodman thin-disk solutions and steady-state migration regimes.

analysis.reason: The paper investigates the theoretical hydrodynamics of advection-dominated accretion flows (ADAF) around black holes in Eddington-inspired Born-Infeld (EiBI) modified gravity, which lacks direct application to high-energy transients, FRBs, supernovae engines, or relativistic jets.
analysis.result: In the $s=-1$ branch of EiBI gravity, the ADAF-like flow exhibits systematically lower radial velocity $v_{r}$, sound speed $c_{s}$, specific angular momentum $l$, and temperature $T$, alongside higher density $\rho$ and disk scale height $H$ compared to standard Paczyński-Wiita (PW) gravity. The sonic point shifts inward from $r_{\rm sp} \simeq 3.7673\,r_{s}$ to $3.6072\,r_{s}$. Furthermore, the normalized mass accretion rate $\dot{M}/\dot{M}_{\rm B}$ varies from $\simeq 0.054$ to $\simeq 0.058$ as the core radius $r_{c}$ increases, but decreases from $\simeq 0.054$ to $\simeq 0.045$ as the charge parameter $r_{q}$ increases.
analysis.problem: Evaluating how deviations from General Relativity in the strong-field regime, specifically under Palatini Eddington-inspired Born-Infeld gravity, modify the hydrodynamic and thermodynamic structure of low-angular-momentum transonic accretion flows onto black holes.
analysis.method: Constructed an effective Paczyński-Wiita-like pseudo-Newtonian potential $\Phi_{\rm PW}(r) = -\left(1+\frac{s r_{c}^{4}}{x(r)^{4}}\right)\left(\frac{r_{s}x(r)-r_{q}^{2}}{-r_{s}x(r)+x(r)^{2}+r_{q}^{2}}+1\right)$ mapped from static spherically symmetric black hole solutions in EiBI gravity, coupled with stationary, axisymmetric ADAF hydrodynamic equations with Shakura-Sunyaev viscosity $\nu = \alpha c_{s}^{2}/\Omega_{K}$, solved as a two-point boundary value problem using a relaxation method.
citation_leads: Effects of Eddington-inspired Born–Infeld Gravity on Black Hole Accretion: “Black holes offer a unique setting to test gravity in the strong-field regime, where deviations from General Relativity are expected to be most pronounced.”
II.3 PW-like potential: “The pseudo-Newtonian potential is chosen so that the extrema of the Newtonian effective potential coincide with those for timelike geodesics of the spacetime.”

IV Results: “Compared with the standard PW case, the EiBI gravity solution predicts lower $v_{r}$, $c_{s}$, $l$, and $T$ over most of the accretion flow. In contrast, $\rho$ and $H$ increase systematically.”

analysis.reason: This work quantitatively establishes how static shear strains exponentially accelerate self-diffusion in Yukawa crystals via Frenkel pair nucleation, providing key microphysical inputs for magnetar crustal creep, stress relaxation, and burst trigger mechanics.
analysis.result: Static shear strain $\varepsilon$ exponentially enhances self-diffusion by lowering the activation energy barrier for Frenkel defect pair formation via the stored elastic strain energy $\sigma = \frac{1}{2}\mu\varepsilon^2$ within an activation volume $V^*$ containing $N_{\rm act} \equiv n_i V^* \approx 31 \pm 1$ ions across astrophysically relevant screenings ($\kappa \lesssim 1$). The modified diffusion coefficient follows $D(\Gamma^*,\varepsilon) = D_0(\Gamma^*) \exp\left[\frac{1}{2} N_{\rm act} \tilde{\mu} \Gamma \varepsilon^2\right]$, which scales near melting as $D(\Gamma^*,\varepsilon) = \frac{787}{\Gamma^*} \exp\left[-\left(20 - 5\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{0.1}\right)^2\right)\Gamma^*\right]$, increasing diffusion by orders of magnitude at high coupling $\Gamma^*$.
analysis.problem: Understanding whether and how static elastic shear stress alters self-diffusion in body-centered cubic (bcc) Yukawa crystals relevant to neutron star crusts and white dwarf interiors, specifically differentiating whether strain modifies defect migration mobility or defect pair nucleation rates.
analysis.method: Performed classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations of bcc Yukawa crystals with frozen boundary layers under static $xy$-shear strain using LAMMPS, tracking ion mean-squared displacements (MSDs) across various coupling parameters $\Gamma^*$ and screening parameters $\kappa$ to extract defect nucleation rates $\nu(\varepsilon)$ and activation volumes $V^*$.
citation_leads: Stress-enhanced diffusion in Yukawa crystals: “We simulate sheared Yukawa crystals and show that a static elastic strain exponentially enhances diffusion due to the additional elastic energy stored in the region that participates in Frenkel pair formation relative to the unstrained”
IV Results: “This is perhaps the most useful key result of this work, namely, that $N_{\rm act}\approx 31\pm 1$ holds across astrophysically relevant screenings.”

V Discussion: “In magnetars, magnetic stresses drive the crust toward failure; stress-enhanced diffusion in the most strained regions opens a channel for thermally activated creep and gradual stress relaxation”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrated that strain acts exclusively on the Arrhenius defect nucleation rate $\ln[\nu(\varepsilon)/\nu_0] = \frac{1}{2} N_{\rm act} \tilde{\mu} \Gamma \varepsilon^2$ rather than defect hopping speed, confirming a universal activation particle number $N_{\rm act} \approx 31$ that corresponds to the first two neighbor shells of the bcc lattice.

analysis.reason: The paper directly addresses prompt coherent radio counterpart searches (FRB-like emission) from compact binary coalescences using gravitational-wave early warnings, combining RL-based telescope pointing optimization with DSA and the Chronoscope backend.
analysis.problem: Optimizing slewing and pointing schedules for single-pointing array telescopes (DSA) under rapidly evolving, uncertain gravitational-wave early-warning localization maps to capture millisecond-duration prompt coherent radio bursts around compact binary coalescences.
analysis.method: Formulated a finite-horizon Markov Decision Process from $t=-60\,\mathrm{s}$ to $+20\,\mathrm{s}$ discretized at $\Delta t = 1\,\mathrm{s}$ using PPO (Proximal Policy Optimization) on simulated O5 HLV early-warning localization sequences (BAYESTAR at 29, 38, 56, and 1024 Hz), gated by a classifier/regression model dispatch, and validated trajectory tracking on prototype DSA antennas at OVRO with azimuth slew rates up to $3.8^\circ\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$.
assumptions: Array dishes share a single unified pointing trajectory with a circular top-hat effective field of view of $\sim 18\,\mathrm{deg}^2$ and elevation cutoff $\ge 20^\circ$.

analysis.result:
GRB 241113B is confirmed as an intrinsically soft Type II GRB (XRR/XRF) observed on-axis within a redshift range $0.5 \lesssim z \lesssim 3.5$. Joint prompt spectral fitting favors a cutoff power-law (CPL) model with photon index $\alpha = -1.80^{+0.16}_{-0.10}$ and $E^{\mathrm{obs}}_{\mathrm{peak}} \approx 35	ext{--}37	ext{ keV}$. The prompt duration follows an energy-dependent scaling law $\log T_{90} = \alpha \log(E/50\,\mathrm{keV}) + \log K_{50}$ with $\alpha = -0.35^{+0.10}_{-0.06}$ ($K_{50} = 54.2^{+2.8}_{-4.2}$). The early multiband afterglow peaks at deceleration time $t_b = 263^{+68}_{-91}\,\mathrm{s}$ and decays with $\alpha_2 = -1.40^{+0.03}_{-0.04}$ and spectral index $ eta_{\mathrm{OX}} = 0.66^{+0.04}_{-0.03}$. VegasAfterglow modeling confirms a relativistic top-hat jet propagating into a wind-like circumstellar medium ($s=2$) in the slow cooling regime ($
u_m < 
u_{\mathrm{opt}} < 
u_{\mathrm{X}} < 
u_c$) with electron index $p = 2.31 \pm 0.08$. The bulk Lorentz factor is constrained to $\Gamma_0 > 100$ (posterior bounds $\Gamma_0 \sim 125	ext{--}263$), ruling out both shock breakout (SBO) and high baryon loading (dirty fireball) scenarios.
analysis.problem: Unveiling the physical origin of prompt spectral softness in X-ray rich bursts (XRR) and X-ray flashes (XRF): whether they are driven by geometric viewing angle effects (off-axis jets), relativistic shock breakouts, dirty fireballs with heavy baryon loading ($\Gamma_0 \ll 100$), or intrinsic jet dissipative processes.
analysis.method: Joint prompt spectral fitting across 0.5–1000 keV combining EP/WXT, SVOM/ECLAIRs, and SVOM/GRM with PL, CPL, and Band models. analysis.result: Dynamic radial stability is strictly governed by the fundamental mode frequency $\omega_0^2 > 0$. Strong repulsive self-interaction ($y=10^3$) yields a stiffer dark matter equation of state that supports extended dark halos around compact ordinary matter cores, with maximum stable masses scaling as $M_{\rm max} \propto m_f^{-2}$, reaching up to $66.79 M_\odot$ for $m_f = 2\ \mathrm{GeV}$, $10.69 M_\odot$ for $m_f = 5\ \mathrm{GeV}$, and $2.672 M_\odot$ for $m_f = 10\ \mathrm{GeV}$. The gravitational redshift at the visible ordinary matter surface is given by $1+z_{\mathrm{OM}} = e^{\Delta\Phi_{\rm halo}}/\sqrt{1-2M/R}$ where $\Delta\Phi_{\rm halo} = \int_{R_{\mathrm{OM}}}^{R}[m(r)+4\pi r^{3}p(r)]/[r(r-2m(r))]\,\mathrm{d}r$, allowing stable configurations to exceed the standard vacuum Buchdahl redshift limit ($z=2$).

analysis.reason: It addresses the rapid identification and ranking of kilonova counterparts to gravitational-wave (GW) triggers in large-scale optical surveys like Vera C. Rubin/LSST, directly serving compact object multimessenger follow-up.
analysis.result: In candidate galleries containing 5000 transients, MAGIKS achieves a Recall@1 of $39.8\%$ (compared to $4.8\%$ for optical-only and $0.2\%$ for sky-localization-only baselines) and an MRR of $0.488$; for GW170817 under Rubin observing conditions, Recall@1 reaches $87.3\%$ and Recall@10 reaches $95.7\%$, while pairwise binary classification yields an AUROC of $0.983$ and an accuracy of $0.942$.
analysis.problem: Wide-field optical searches following GW triggers (BNS and NSBH mergers) are heavily contaminated by thousands of spatio-temporally compatible non-kilonova transients (e.g., SNe, AGNs, TDEs), where pure optical classification or spatial sky-map priors alone fail to jointly assess physical consistency.
analysis.method: An align-before-fuse multimodal architecture that combines a GW encoder (MLP for 7 scalar parameters including $\mathcal{M}_c^{\rm det}$, spins, $\cos\iota$, and $d_L$, plus a 1D-CNN for 3D sky maps) and an optical encoder (modified mTAN with SNR-biased attention for irregular multiband light curves), pre-aligned via time-aware contrastive loss and fused via dual cross-attention conditioned on physical ejecta properties $\bm{\psi} = (\log_{10}(M_{\rm dyn}/M_\odot), \log_{10}(M_{\rm wind}/M_\odot), |\cos\iota|, \log_{10}(d_L/\mathrm{Gpc}))$.
citation_leads: MAGIKS: Multimodal Alignment and Gravitational-Wave-Conditioned Interaction for Kilonova Search: “In the largest evaluated galleries, each containing 5000 candidates, MAGIKS ranks the true counterpart first for 39.8% of queries, compared with 4.8% for optical-only ranking and 0.2% for sky-localization-only ranking.”
IV.2 Retrieval ablations: “In the variant without cross-attention, the cross-attention fusion mechanism is replaced by concatenating the encoder feature vectors before the classification head.”

IV.4 Classification ablation experiments: “MAGIKS provides the strongest overall classification performance, with AUROC of 0.983, AUPRC of 0.951, accuracy of 0.942, precision of 0.877, and $F_{1}$ of 0.885.”

IV.5 Sensitivity to individual GW parameters: “We construct a physics-informed empirical bridge as a data-driven reference for the physical associations accessible to MAGIKS. Without using a deep-learning model, the bridge maps the GW query and the optical light curve independently”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates that conditioning optical counterpart ranking on GW scalar posteriors and sky maps simultaneously improves candidate retrieval efficiency by nearly an order of magnitude over optical-only classifiers in dense contaminant fields ($N = 5000$).

figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview of the proposed multimodal framework for gravitational-wave-triggered kilonova counterpart search. The upper stream encodes the gravitational-wave trigger using source-parameter descriptors and the sky-localization map: scalar parameters are projected with a multilayer perceptron (MLP), while the skymap is processed by a one-dimensional convolutional network and pooled into a localization feature. The lower stream encodes Rubin/LSST optical alerts using irregularly sampled multiband light curves and sky coordinates: temporal samples are represented on a reference time grid with time embeddings and encoded by the Multi-Time Attention Network (mTAN) module, while coordinates are encoded separately. The contrastive-learning branch projects the gravitational-wave and optical representations into a shared embedding space and uses a supervised contrastive objective with a time-compatibility term to favour physically plausible pairs. The fusion branch performs two explicit cross-modal matching operations, comparing optical coordinates with the gravitational-wave localization and gravitational-wave source descriptors with the optical temporal evolution, and produces the final ranking score for counterpart retrieval.
figures.label: Fig. 1

analysis.reason: This work explores how a first-order quark-hadron phase transition (PT) in core-collapse supernovae naturally generates the observed high-mass peak ($1.55\text{--}1.72\,M_\odot$) of neutron stars through accretion delay before the second collapse.
analysis.result: The phase transition triggers a second collapse and shock wave, with the delay time $\Delta t_{\mathrm{collapse}}$ anti-correlating with progenitor compactness $\xi_{1.75}$. Lower-compactness progenitors accrete longer before reaching the PT onset density, leaving heavier remnants and naturally concentrating neutron star gravitational masses into narrow high-mass peaks at $\sim 1.70\,M_\odot$ (RDF1.1, ranging $1.66\text{--}1.72\,M_\odot$) or $1.55\text{--}1.70\,M_\odot$ (RDF1.2). The critical compactness dividing explosion from black hole formation is $\xi_{1.75} \sim 0.59\text{--}0.69$ for RDF1.1 and $\sim 1.04\text{--}1.07$ for RDF1.2.

analysis.problem: Observed neutron star mass distributions show a bimodal structure with a high-mass peak around $1.75\text{--}1.8\,M_\odot$, which standard neutrino-driven core-collapse supernova simulations typically fail to reproduce because high-compactness progenitors usually collapse directly into black holes rather than exploding.
analysis.method: Performed systematic 1D general-relativistic hydrodynamic simulations using the `GR1D` code with M1 neutrino transport across solar-metallicity progenitors ($13\text{--}120\,M_\odot$, with step $\Delta M = 0.2\,M_\odot$ for $13\text{--}30\,M_\odot$). Used hybrid equations of state (RDF1.1 and RDF1.2) combining DD2 with a relativistic density functional quark model with onset thresholds $\rho_{\mathrm{onset}} \approx 4.07 \times 10^{14}\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ ($M_{\mathrm{onset}} \approx 1.60\,M_\odot$) and $\rho_{\mathrm{onset}} \approx 3.15 \times 10^{14}\,\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ ($M_{\mathrm{onset}} \approx 1.44\,M_\odot$). Compactness was defined via $\xi_M = \frac{M / M_\odot}{R(M_{\mathrm{bary}} = M) / (1000\,\mathrm{km})}$.

analysis.reason: The study demonstrates that structured jets substantially enhance off-axis very-high-energy (VHE) external inverse-Compton (EIC) emission from short GRBs compared to top-hat jets, offering critical multi-messenger detection prospects for CTAO and gravitational wave follow-ups.
analysis.result: Structured jets (Gaussian and power-law) yield much stronger off-axis $1\,\mathrm{TeV}$ EIC emission than top-hat jets due to relativistic beaming and lateral energy profiles. In the coasting phase with constant seed photon luminosity, the EIC flux scales as $F_{\varepsilon}^{\rm EIC} \propto T$ in the Thomson regime for $\varepsilon_m^{\rm EIC} < \varepsilon < \varepsilon_c^{\rm EIC}$, and rapidly decays as $F_{\varepsilon}^{\rm EIC} \propto T^{-33/7}$ at $T \gtrsim T_a \sim 300\,\mathrm{s}$, whereas synchrotron self-Compton (SSC) emission rises sharply as $F_{\varepsilon}^{\rm SSC} \propto T^4$ before dominating after the deceleration stage ($T \sim 5 \times 10^3\,\mathrm{s}$).
analysis.problem: Whether off-axis short GRBs can produce detectable VHE gamma rays via EIC scattering of extended emission, X-ray plateau, or kilonova seed photons within realistic structured jet geometries.
analysis.method: Numerical modeling using the AMES code integrating emissions over equal-arrival-time surfaces, incorporating Klein-Nishina suppression, forward shock relativistic electron dynamics, and external seed photon fields characterized by broken power-law spectra ($G(\varepsilon)$ with break $\varepsilon_b = E_b / \Gamma$, $\beta_1 = 0.5$, $\beta_2 = 2.0$) and temporal luminosity decay $L(T) \propto T^{-\alpha}$.

analysis.result: SN 2025dys reached a peak bolometric luminosity of $L = (8.57\pm 0.41)\times 10^{42}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ with early X-ray emission detected at $L_{\rm X} \approx 7.55\times 10^{40}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. Modeling with CSI and radioactive decay requires an ejecta mass $M_{\rm ej} \approx 2.45\text{--}2.69\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$, kinetic energy $E_{\rm K} \approx 0.37\text{--}0.46\,\mathrm{foe}$, circumstellar medium mass $M_{\rm CSM} \approx 0.54\text{--}0.76\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$, and an optical depth of $\tau_{\rm CSM} = 13$ from early electron-scattering wings.
analysis.problem: Unraveling whether the high peak luminosity and spectral evolution of the peculiar transient SN 2025dys are driven by radioactive decay, a central magnetar engine, or shock interaction with a confined, dense circumstellar medium around a stripped-envelope progenitor.
analysis.method: Multi-band photometry fitting via MOSFiT testing pure radioactive decay ($s=0, 2$), magnetar engine, and CSI+RD models, combined with early electron-scattering profile modeling using Monte Carlo radiative transfer and Swift-XRT X-ray analysis.
assumptions: Electron scattering in the unshocked dense CSM dominates the Lorentzian-like wing profile in the earliest optical spectra.
limits: Pure radioactive decay and pure magnetar-driven models fail to match observed multi-color light curves and physical progenitor constraints.

analysis.result: The 35-day precessional period exhibits a secular decline with $\dot{P}_{35} \approx (-5.04 \pm 0.1) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$ as measured by RXTE/ASM and MAXI, and piecewise rates of $(-1.3 \pm 0.2) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$ and $(-4.7 \pm 0.1) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$ separated by the anomalous low state (ALS) at MJD 51500, matching the theoretical prediction of accretion-driven moment-of-inertia evolution $\dot{P}_{\rm pr}/P_{\rm pr} \approx -(\dot{\Delta I})/\Delta I \sim -\frac{1}{4}(\dot{M}/M_{\rm NS})(P_{\rm pr}/P_*) \sim -2\times 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}$ yielding $\dot{P}_{\rm pr} \sim -6\times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$.

analysis.problem: Whether the 35-day super-orbital cycle in Her X-1 is purely governed by chaotic accretion disk precession or paced by a quasi-stable underlying clock mechanism such as neutron star free precession.
analysis.method: Multi-mission X-ray light curve analysis (CGRO/BATSE, RXTE/ASM, Swift/BAT, Fermi/GBM, MAXI) spanning over 50 years using sliding-window phase averaging and parabolic $O-C$ phase fitting: $\phi(t) = \phi_0(T_0) + \frac{P_{35} - P_0}{P_0 P_{35}}(t - T_0) + \frac{\dot{P}_{35}}{2 P_{35}^2}(t - T_0)^2$, combined with a biaxial neutron star free precession model governed by $\frac{\dot{P}_{\mathrm{pr}}}{P_{\mathrm{pr}}}=\frac{\dot{P}_{*}}{P_{*}}+\frac{\dot{I}_{3}}{I_{3}}-\frac{\dot{(\Delta I)}}{\Delta I}+(\tan\theta)\dot{\theta}$.
assumptions: The 35-day X-ray cycle is paced by the free precession of a biaxial neutron star whose oblateness evolves due to steady accretion.
limits: During anomalous low states (ALS), outer disk synchronization with the neutron star precession is temporarily lost, causing discrete period jumps.
citation_leads: 2.1 35-day period evolution using RXTE/ASM - Swift/BAT - MAXI X-ray light curve: “The result is $\dot{P}_{35}\approx(-5.04\pm 0.1)\times 10^{-5}$ s s-1.”

3 Discussion and conclusion: “During the ALS the outer parts of the accretion disk is thought to move toward

analysis.result: A high-energy spectral excess at $\sim 30$–$500\,\mathrm{GeV}$ is detected at $\sim 7.90\sigma$ significance ($\Delta\mathrm{TS}=72.34$). analysis.reason: This work performs an unprecedented multi-wavelength pulse profile modeling (PPM) of the nearest millisecond pulsar PSR J0437-4715 combining HST, NICER, XMM-Newton, and NuSTAR datasets to obtain the tightest neutron star radius and equation of state constraints to date.
analysis.result: Using the ST+PDT+EL+PL surface emission configuration, the headline PPM inference yields an equatorial radius of $R_{\rm eq} = 11.35_{-0.39}^{+0.40}\,\mathrm{km}$ (or $R_{\rm eq} = 11.345_{-0.388}^{+0.399}\,\mathrm{km}$) and a mass of $M = 1.377_{-0.034}^{+0.038}\,M_{\odot}$. The whole-surface warm emission has an effective temperature in the stellar frame of $\log_{10}(T_{\rm else}\,[\mathrm{K}]) = 5.451 \pm 0.008$ ($T_{\rm else} = (2.82 \pm 0.05) \times 10^{5}\,\mathrm{K}$), translating to an observer at infinity to $T_{\rm else}^{\infty} = T_{\rm else}/(1+z) = (2.26 \pm 0.03) \times 10^{5}\,\mathrm{K}$ via the gravitational redshift $1+z = \left(1 - \frac{2GM}{R_{\rm eq}c^2}\right)^{-1/2}$, with observed flux scaling as $F \propto (R_{\rm eq}^{\infty}/d)^2 \sigma (T_{\rm else}^{\infty})^4$. The pulsed non-thermal power-law component exhibits photon index $\Gamma_{\rm PL} = 1.310_{-0.061}^{+0.054}$ and pulsed amplitude $A_{\rm PL} = 0.684_{-0.057}^{+0.059}$. At the 95% credibility level, the upper limit of the neutron star radius is reduced by $\approx 0.4\text{--}0.6\,\mathrm{km}$, yielding inferred radius at $1.4\,M_{\odot}$ of $R_{1.4} = 11.52_{-0.50}^{+0.66}\,\mathrm{km}$ (piecewise polytrope) and $11.48_{-0.52}^{+0.61}\,\mathrm{km}$ (speed of sound), ruling out stiff EOSs with $R > 12.0\,\mathrm{km}$ at 68% credibility.
analysis.problem: Previous radius inferences of PSR J0437-4715 suffered from strong degeneracies between the pulsed non-thermal magnetospheric power-law tail, the soft thermal hot spots, and the diffuse warm stellar surface. Without joint far-UV (HST) and hard X-ray (NuSTAR) coverage, the non-thermal normalization and whole-surface emission were unconstrained, leading to divergent radius posteriors ranging from $\sim 7.9\,\mathrm{km}$ up to $\sim 14.1\,\mathrm{km}$.
analysis.method: The authors perform multi-wavelength pulse profile modeling within an extended X-PSI Bayesian inference framework over $0.007\text{--}16.0\,\mathrm{keV}$, integrating $2.56\,\mathrm{Ms}$ of NICER XTI data, $113\,\mathrm{ks}$ of XMM-Newton EPIC MOS data, $221\,\mathrm{ks}$ of NuSTAR FPM data ($3.0\text{--}16.0\,\mathrm{keV}$), and HST STIS far-UV spectroscopy ($1150\text{--}1700\,\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$). The likelihood couples a modified Gaussian log-likelihood for HST STIS fluxes $\mathcal{L}(\theta,\mathbf{B})=\sum_{i,k}\left[\frac{(c_{ik}(\theta)-d_{ik}+B_{i}T_{\rm exp}\int_{\phi_{k}}d\phi)^2}{\sigma_{ik}^2}+\ln(2\pi\sigma_{ik}^2)\right]$ with Poisson likelihoods for X-ray timing data. The geometric model combines a northern single-temperature (ST) hydrogen atmosphere spot (NSXH), an equatorial/southern protruding dual-temperature (PDT) spot, an unheated warm surface (EL) with partially ionized hydrogen (NSXHp), and an observer-frame sinusoidally modulated power law $F(E,\phi)=N_{\mathrm{PL}}(E/1\,\mathrm{keV})^{-\Gamma_{\mathrm{PL}}}[1+A_{\mathrm{PL}}\cos(2\pi(\phi-\phi_{\mathrm{PL}}))]$ evaluated using MultiNest nested sampling.
assumptions: The warm unheated stellar surface emits as a partially ionized hydrogen atmosphere (NSXHp) at uniform effective temperature $T_{\rm else}$ over the region outside the hot spots.

IV.1.2 ST-U+EL: “We then include the EL component with NSXHp to describe the rest of the warm surface in this ST-U+EL model.”
IV.1.4 Spectral rebinning in X-PSI: “Overall, the implemented spectral binning preserves the fit quality and provides accelerated likelihood calculations.”
V.2 Implications for the dense matter EOS: “where the upper limit of the radius is reduced by approximately 0.4–0.6 km.”
VI.3 The thermal properties of the NS warm surface: “translates to $T_{\rm else}^{\infty}=(2.26\pm 0.03)\,\times 10^{5}$ K.”
VIII Conclusion and future work: “The results are consistent with the PPM measurements of two other MSPs of similar mass”
analysis.research_progress: By simultaneously resolving the degeneracy between compactness $M/R_{\rm eq}$ (from soft X-ray pulse profiles) and redshifted radiation radius $R_{\rm eq}^{\infty} = R_{\rm eq}\left(1 - \frac{2GM}{R_{\rm eq}c^2}\right)^{-1/2}$ (from FUV flux constraints), this work eliminates the bimodal posterior around $12\,\mathrm{km}$, narrows the radius credible interval to $\pm 0.40\,\mathrm{km}$, and brings PSR J0437-4715 into close agreement with PPM measurements of PSR J0030+0451 and PSR J0614-3329.

analysis.reason: The paper investigates the physical conditions required to form micron-sized presolar graphite grains in supernova ejecta, providing key scaling relations linking grain sizes to explosion energy, ejecta mass, progenitor radius, and nickel heating.
analysis.result: In Ni-free ejecta undergoing matter-dominated adiabatic expansion, the final graphite grain radius scales analytically as $r_{\rm gr,final} \simeq 615\,\mu\mathrm{m}\,(E_{\rm exp}/10^{48}\,\mathrm{erg})^{-3/2}\,(M_{\rm ej}/5\,M_\odot)^{5/2}\,(R_0/10^{12}\,\mathrm{cm})^{-2}\,(X'_{\rm C}/3\times 10^{-3})$, governed by the local key parameter combination $X'_{\rm C}\rho_{2000}\tau_{\rm cool,2000} \propto X'_{\rm C}E_{\rm exp}^{-3/2}M_{\rm ej}^{5/2}R_0^{-2}$. Micron-sized grains ($r_{\rm gr} \gtrsim 1\,\mu\mathrm{m}$) require low explosion energy ($E_{\rm exp} \lesssim 10^{49}\text{--}10^{50}\,\mathrm{erg}$), massive ejecta, and negligible radioactive $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ heating, as $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}$ heating delays dust condensation until the ejecta expands to much lower densities, suppressing final grain radii below $0.1\,\mu\mathrm{m}$.

analysis.problem: Presolar graphite grains extracted from meteorites exhibit supernova isotopic signatures and reach sizes $\gtrsim 1\,\mu\mathrm{m}$, whereas standard core-collapse supernova models ($E_{\rm exp} \sim 10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$, $M_{\rm ej} \sim 10\,M_\odot$, $M_{\rm Ni} \sim 0.01\text{--}0.1\,M_\odot$) typically predict graphite grain sizes below $0.1\,\mu\mathrm{m}$.
analysis.method: A spherical, uniformly expanding one-zone ejecta dynamics model coupled to an energy equation including radioactive $^{56}\mathrm{Ni}\rightarrow{}^{56}\mathrm{Co}\rightarrow{}^{56}\mathrm{Fe}$ decay heating $\dot{Q}$, $p\,dV$ work, and radiative cooling. Dust formation is calculated using classical homogeneous nucleation theory for carbon monomers and moment equations $dK_j^{(\ell)}/dt$ coupled to key species depletion, with analytical scaling relations derived for the matter-dominated adiabatic limit ($T \propto \rho^{2/3}$) at the reference condensation temperature $T = 2000\,\mathrm{K}$.
assumptions: Constant carbon sticking probability $\alpha_{\rm C} = 1$ and pre-set effective carbon mass fraction $X'_{\rm C}$ assuming molecular CO formation locks up equal parts of carbon and oxygen without solving explicit time-dependent chemical networks.
limits: Calculations do not resolve the multi-dimensional density and composition structure, clumping, or radioactive chemical destruction within real supernova ejecta.

analysis.result: Optical linear polarisation is detected at $P = 0.3\text{--}1.5\%$ across $R$ and $I$ bands. analysis.reason: This study accurately computes non-thermal electron impact ionization cross sections for Sr and investigates excitation-autoionization (EAI) and inner-shell Auger cascades, which directly impacts non-LTE ionization modeling of kilonova ejecta.
analysis.result: Excitation-autoionization (EAI) constitutes roughly half of the total single ionization cross sections for $\mathrm{Sr\,I}$ and $\mathrm{Sr\,II}$, and omitting EAI leads to an error factor of up to $\sim 2$ in the derived ion abundances. Inner-shell ionization accounts for $30\% - 40\%$ of the total cross section in $\mathrm{Sr\,I}$ and $20\% - 30\%$ in $\mathrm{Sr\,II-III}$ at $5\,\mathrm{keV}$, scaling as $\propto \ln(E)/E$ at high energies; incorporating inner-shell ionization and Auger cascades modifies ion fractions by $20\% - 50\%$. Furthermore, approximately $20\% - 30\%$ of heavy atoms (e.g., Te) are ionized beyond triply ionized states at kilonova ejecta temperatures.
analysis.problem: Standard kilonova spectral synthesis often relies on empirical Lotz cross sections ($\sigma_{\mathrm{Lotz}}(E) = \sum_i n_i a_i \frac{\ln(E/I_i)}{E I_i}$) that neglect excitation-autoionization (EAI) and inner-shell multi-electron ejection via Auger cascades, introducing significant systematic errors into non-thermal ionization balance and line identification.
analysis.method: Level-resolved (J-split) and configuration-average (CA) electron impact cross sections were computed using the Flexible Atomic Code (FAC) with distorted wave and binary encounter dipole approximations up to $5\,\mathrm{keV}$. These cross sections were integrated into the `pynonthermal` Spencer-Fano solver under an energy deposition rate $q(t) = 0.15 \,(t / 1.4\,\mathrm{days})^{-1.3}\,\mathrm{eV\,s^{-1}\,ion^{-1}}$ to iteratively solve for the degraded electron spectrum $y(E)$ and the non-thermal steady-state ionization balance $\sum_{i \le j} \sum_{k > j-i} n_i \Gamma_{i,k} = n_{j+1} n_e \alpha_{j+1}(T)$.
assumptions: Steady-state balance between non-thermal collisional ionization and radiative/dielectronic recombination in the ejecta
limits: Photoionization, thermal collisional ionization, and charge exchange reactions are omitted from the Spencer-Fano model
citation_leads: 3.1. Single Ionization: Sr I: “The Lotz ionization cross section agrees well near the ionization threshold but fails to account for the enhanced cross section due to excitationautoionization.”

4.1. Spencer-Fano Implementation: “The above ionization balance includes only non-thermal ionization and the supplied recombination rates. Photoionization, thermal collisional ionization, and charge exchange are omitted.”

4.5. Extrapolation to Higher Ion Stages: “full model extrapolated to higher charge states shows that approximately 20 - 30% of the Te atoms are found in charge states above triply ionized at the temperatures expected in KNe ejecta.”
6. Conclusions: “conversion of near-neutral inner shell ionization cross sections into finalion-resolved cross sections leads to changes in near-neutral ion fractions of order 20-50%.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrated that threshold binning can compress $>10^5$ cross-section channels down to $\sim 35$ with negligible precision loss ($<5\%$), provided complete EAI and inner-shell cross sections for $\mathrm{Sr\,I-III}$, and established the necessity of extending kilonova ionization models to higher charge states (e.g., Te XI).

analysis.reason: This paper presents the Fourier power spectrum injection framework and empirical sensitivity calibration for the CHIME All-sky Multiday Pulsar Stacking Search (CHAMPSS), characterizing pulse smearing, FDMT chromatic artifacts, and red noise limits relevant to blind pulsar and periodic transient searches.
analysis.result: For stacking depths of 1–30 days, CHAMPSS achieves maximum sensitivity for pulsar spin frequencies $f \approx 0.1\text{--}100\,\mathrm{Hz}$ and flux densities $S \gtrsim 1\,\mathrm{mJy}$. Monthly incoherent stacking increases the transmission fraction of faint sources ($0.1 < S < 1\,\mathrm{mJy}$) by up to $50\%$ (from $0.08\%$ in daily searches to $6.6\%$ in month-long searches). Both coherent and incoherent stacking scale in detection significance as $S_{\mathrm{min}} \propto N_{\mathrm{days}}^{-1/2}$, but red noise degrades the sensitivity at long periods ($P \gtrsim 1\,\mathrm{s}$, $f \lesssim 0.1\,\mathrm{Hz}$) by an order of magnitude compared to standard radiometer equation predictions.
analysis.problem: Quantifying the search completeness and selection effects of all-sky pulsar stacking searches without computationally prohibitive and irreversible raw time-domain signal injections, while accounting for non-astrophysical red noise, scalloping loss, and Fast Dispersion Measure Transform (FDMT) covariance artifacts.
analysis.method: Synthetic signal injection directly into Fourier power spectra across parameter grids of spin frequency $f \in [10^{-3}, 10^{2.7}]\,\mathrm{Hz}$, $\mathrm{DM}$, and flux density $S \in [0.001, 10]\,\mathrm{mJy}$. The pipeline incorporates normalized profile scaling $A = \frac{GS}{(T_{\mathrm{sys}}+T_{\mathrm{sky}})\beta}\sqrt{\frac{n_{\mathrm{days}}}{N_k}}\sqrt{N_{\mathrm{pol}}\Delta\nu\tau}$, effective temporal smearing $\Delta t_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx \sqrt{1.25\Delta t_{\mathrm{samp}}^2 + \Delta t_{\mathrm{dedisp}}^2 + \Delta t_{\mathrm{chan}}^2}$, sinc-squared scalloping attenuation $P_j = |a_j|^2 \mathrm{sinc}^2[\pi(r-j)]$, running median red noise normalization, and DBSCAN candidate clustering.
citation_leads: CHIME All-sky Multiday Pulsar Stacking Search (CHAMPSS): Power Spectrum Injections and Survey SensitivityFacilities: CHIME, Calcul Québec: “For stacks of depths 1$-$30 days, CHAMPSS is most sensitive to pulsars with frequencies on the order of 0.1$-$100 Hz and flux densities $\gtrsim 1$ mJy.”
III.2 Pulse Smearing Effects: “This smearing is a convolution in the time domain of the raw sample time $\Delta t_{samp}$ with a set of functions representing the different sources of smearing”

V.1 Single-Parameter Injection Results: “Regardless of their other parameters, only $\sim$ 0.08% of our “core” injections with $S<0.1$ mJy survive to the candidate stage for the daily search. In the month-long search, this value increases to 6.6%.”
Appendix B Noise in CHAMPSS: “Given the impact of red noise on pulsar searching, we encourage analysis of red noise at different radio telescopes to assist in survey planning.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrated that power spectrum injection accurately maps multi-parameter survey sensitivity curves, proved the theoretical scaling $S_{\mathrm{min}} \propto N_{\mathrm{days}}^{-1/2}$ for both coherent and incoherent stacking regimes, and revealed empirical sensitivity turnover in galactic-plane regions when $N_{\mathrm{days}} \gtrsim 25$.

figures.caption: Figure 6: This plot shows the difference in transmissivity $p_{\text{single}}-p_{\text{stack}}$ integrated over our “core” distribution. As we increase the stack depth, we gain transmissivity in most of our parameter space. The exceptions are at $f\lesssim 0.1$ Hz and $S\gtrsim 1$ mJy, where we actually lose transmissivity by stacking a month of power spectra. We attribute these drop-offs to increased red noise in month-long stacks and RFI clustering respectively.

figures.physical_core: Stacking generally increases transmissivity across the core parameter space, but reduces it for $f\lesssim 0.1\,\mathrm{Hz}$ and $S\gtrsim 1\,\mathrm{mJy}$. The paper attributes these losses to increased red noise in month-long stacks and RFI clustering, respectively.

figures.caption: Figure 7: The left-hand plot shows our minimum detectable flux density threshold as a function of number of days in the stack, while the right-hand plot shows the same quantity as a function of spin period. The bold lines represent the flux density threshold where we retrieve $\geq 50$ % of our injections, and the shaded areas of the radiometer equation run from the minimum to maximum DM expected for a given channelization, and from a spin frequency of 1 Hz to one of 250 Hz in the left-hand plot. For the radiometer equation regions, we used an SNR of 7 for comparison with Figure 5 in [ 1 ] and a $\delta$ of 2.6% for comparison with Figure 11 in [ 18 ]. We limited injections to $1.5\%\leq\delta\leq 3.6\%$. Our flux density threshold for 50% injection retrieval largely agrees with the radiometer equation [ 20 ] as a function of days in the stack (left), but disagrees as a function of period (right). We attribute this disagreement to the impact of red noise at long periods.
figures.label: Fig. 7
figures.physical_core: The figure compares the 50% injection-retrieval flux-density threshold with radiometer-equation estimates as a function of stack duration and spin period. The thresholds largely agree with the radiometer equation versus stack duration but disagree versus period; the paper attributes the latter discrepancy to red noise at long periods.
